handoff_record.next_agent_notes: Read the revised briefs before claiming AGENT-LOOP-002; §2 lists what the code does today with file:line references. Six findings change the implementation: (1) AgentLoopDriver serves one anchor list and ignores the scene id (AgentLoopDriver.cs:57, :101), so T2 must make anchors per scene; (2) ResolveTarget checks scene node names before anchors (:129), so T5 anchors named after furniture would resolve to mesh centres; (3) WorldView.ShowScene returns nothing and disables the open world before loading the level (WorldView.cs:226, :233), and the --scene pin swallows other requests (:200); (4) on arrival IntentMoveController installs an IdleController (AvatarCharacter.cs:166), and an intent received within ArrivalRadius produces no arrival event, so T3 needs its own arrival hook; (5) the loop avatar's scene and spawn come from the feed (Main.cs:250-251), so with the default replay it spawns at interior coordinates with SceneId personal_1; T1 must own the spawn; (6) spectator doors call ShowScene directly (WorldView.cs:683, :699, :724), so T1 must block them while the loop owns the scene. Also unrecorded: which fixture the 2026-10-17 AGENT-LOOP-001 run used (most likely --fixture open-world-day).
